guide.summary: A fungus that drinks broth and snares passing Siltworms to feed on them for a while.
guide.biology: Some real soil fungi form loops or sticky nets that catch tiny worms and draw food from them.
guide.rules: Stays attached to sediment or mesh and never swims. Eats broth using oxygen. With at least 50 energy and a body at least 1.3 times its starting size, it builds one trap by moving 0.20 carbon into a trap store and spending 8 energy; it will not build one if that would leave it below its starting size. A Siltworm entering its cell is held for 8 seconds, still able to feed but not move, while Traplace drains 0.03 carbon per second from it; half of that becomes Traplace body. A held Siltworm that falls below a quarter of its starting size dies. After letting go, the trap waits 30 seconds before catching again, and Traplace skips broth while draining. New segments grow into free neighboring cells. Comfortable at pH 4.5 to 7, warmth 0.30 to 0.65 and salinity up to 0.25. Fungal inhibitor affects it.
guide.example: Grow Traplace on sediment where Siltworms roam and count how many get caught over a few minutes.
